dns.why: DNS resolves names to addresses (and is itself heavily cached). Encryption is TLS; load balancing and page caching are separate components.

udp-call.why: UDP doesn't retransmit or block on lost packets, which suits real-time media where late data is useless. TCP's reliable, ordered delivery adds waiting.

idempotent-put.why: PUT replaces a resource with the given state, so repeating it changes nothing further. POST typically creates something new each time; PATCH may or may not be idempotent.

created-status.why: 201 says a resource was created (usually with a Location header pointing at it).

push-one-way.why: SSE is a simple one-way stream over HTTP. WebSockets also work but are two-way machinery you don't need; tight polling wastes requests.

reverse-proxy.why: A reverse proxy represents servers to clients. A forward proxy represents clients to the internet.

cdn-dynamic.why: Edge caches cut latency and offload the origin. Personalised, uncacheable responses still go to the origin.
